title: Wood Mackenzie: Geopolitical supply shocks and AI power crunch collide across global base metals
gist: Wood Mackenzie says a data centre pipeline above 250 GW, Middle East smelter damage and US copper stockpiling are colliding with slow mine sanctioning, leaving copper at a record US$14,759/t and aluminium in a 1 Mt 2026 deficit. It also sees nickel splitting into Class I surplus and Class II deficit, and lithium price swings having little effect on storage project costs.

themes.theme: AI power demand and metals intensity

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie tracks more than 250 GW of global data centre projects, over three times the pipeline of a year earlier.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Pipeline growth is the demand driver behind power infrastructure and metals orders.
insights.locator: Wood Mackenzie is tracking more than 250 GW

insights.claim: Transmission networks, substations and dedicated power generation can require three to four times more metal than the data centres they support, creating structural demand beyond the facilities themselves.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: The AI metals impact sits in grid and generation buildout, not just the buildings; favours copper and aluminium exposure.
insights.locator: The metals impact of AI extends well beyond data centres

insights.claim: AI data centre electricity demand is forecast to increase fivefold between 2025 and 2030 and exceed 1,000 TWh by 2035.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Sets the scale of power demand underpinning metals and generation capex.
insights.locator: AI data centre electricity demand is forecast

insights.claim: Asia Pacific data centre power demand is projected to nearly triple by 2030, and grid constraints are pushing operators toward higher-cost microgrid and off-grid solutions.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Grid bottlenecks open a market for on-site generation and storage.
insights.locator: In Asia Pacific, demand is projected to nearly triple

insights.claim: In Japan data centres come online in under five years versus upwards of ten for grid upgrades, driving adoption of microgrids and off-grid generation at two to three times the cost of grid-connected power.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Operators will pay a 2-3x power premium for speed, supporting distributed generation demand.
insights.locator: In Japan, data centres come online in less than five years

insights.claim: Australia has legislated that large-scale data centres must return as much renewable energy to the grid as they draw from it.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A regulatory template that could spread and add renewable demand tied to AI load.
insights.locator: Australia has separately legislated

insights.claim: Copper has hit record prices of US$14,759/t, reflecting severe refined market dislocation.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Record price signals acute physical tightness outside the US.
insights.locator: Copper: Record prices of US$14,759/t

insights.claim: US stockpiling and trade policy have pushed US copper inventory cover above 170 days while the rest of the world has just 48 days and a deficit of about 450-460 kt (the release gives both figures).
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Ex-US shortages and US hoarding mean price spikes and regional premium volatility; watch US trade policy changes.
insights.locator: Physical copper markets remain distorted by US stockpiling

insights.claim: Chilean copper mine output falls 5.2% in 2026, but global mine supply is set to expand by more than 5% next year, ending three years of stagnant growth.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A supply rebound next year could ease the deficit if realised.
insights.locator: Copper: Record prices

insights.claim: The industry must deliver about 850 ktpa of new greenfield copper supply annually over the coming decade, but permitting, geopolitical risk and project complexity constrain development.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Long-run copper tightness depends on sanctioning pace; supports the case for higher-for-longer prices.
insights.locator: Wood Mackenzie estimates the industry must deliver

insights.claim: Despite elevated commodity prices, upstream project sanctioning remains below expectations because of permitting delays, geopolitical uncertainty and growing project complexity.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: High prices are not triggering the usual supply response, which prolongs tightness.
insights.quote: High prices should trigger investment, yet project sanctioning remains below expectations.
insights.locator: Lindsay Grant, Vice President

insights.claim: Attacks in the Middle East damaged two of the world's largest smelters, removing almost 2% of global primary aluminium output and pushing the 2026 balance into a 1 Mt deficit.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Geopolitical damage to smelting capacity is driving the deficit and supports prices and premiums.
insights.locator: The aluminium market faces a supply shock this year

insights.claim: High aluminium prices and premiums plus low alumina costs encouraged smelters to restart idled cells, with Chinese operating rates reaching 99% and output slightly exceeding the national capacity cap.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: China is near its capacity ceiling, limiting further quick supply response.
insights.locator: High aluminium prices and premiums

insights.claim: Indonesian aluminium output reaches 1.3 Mt in 2026 and scales to just under 3 Mt by 2030, but this was not enough to eliminate the 2026 shortfall.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Indonesia is the main swing source of new aluminium supply.
insights.locator: However, this additional volume

insights.claim: Aluminium is projected to return to surplus in 2027 as prices soften, though medium-term fundamentals stay supportive; faster Indonesian expansion and broader economic weakness are the only notable downside risks.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: The 2026 deficit is shock-driven and the downside risks to monitor are Indonesian ramp-up and macro weakness.
insights.locator: While the market is projected to return to surplus in 2027

insights.claim: Global refined nickel output contracts 2% in 2026, the first annual decline since 2015, returning the market toward balance after several years of oversupply.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Marks the end of the multi-year nickel oversupply phase.
insights.locator: The nickel market is returning toward balance in 2026

insights.claim: The nickel Class II segment faces widening deficits from 2027 as Indonesian NPI production consolidates below its 2025 peak under tighter RKAB mining quotas, falling ore grades and El Nino drought disruptions.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Indonesian policy is the key lever for Class II prices; watch RKAB quota decisions.
insights.locator: The Class II segment faces widening deficits

insights.claim: Chinese stainless steel mills are structurally increasing scrap and Class I cathode in melt mixtures to hedge against shrinking NPI availability.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Shifts demand toward Class I and scrap, helping absorb Class I surplus.
insights.locator: In response, Chinese stainless steel mills

insights.claim: Class I and chemical nickel face ongoing surplus from expanding Indonesian HPAL projects and Chinese refining capacity, with sulphur constraints and power bottlenecks as operational risks; prices are forecast to recover toward US$19,000/t by 2030.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Price recovery depends on Indonesian policy and sulphur supply, not on battery demand, which is weak.
insights.locator: Conversely, the Class I and chemical segments

insights.claim: LFP will dominate the mass battery market through 2030, driven by Chinese exports, rapid gigafactory expansion and faster charging; European automakers are pivoting to LFP to preserve margins.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: LFP dominance de-emphasises nickel-rich cathode demand and favours Chinese supply chains.
insights.locator: Battery technology and energy storage

insights.claim: CATL's third-generation Shenxing battery targets a 10% to 80% charge in under four minutes.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Charging-speed gains address a key LFP drawback.
insights.locator: Battery technology and energy storage

insights.claim: In April 2026 CATL secured a three-year, 60 GWh sodium-ion supply agreement with HiTHIUM Energy Storage, with large-scale shipments in China beginning in Q3 2026.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Marks sodium-ion's move to industrial-scale commercialisation, a potential substitute for lithium in storage.
insights.locator: Beyond LFP, alternative chemistries

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie projects sodium-ion and LFP battery module cost parity by 2035, and solid-state mass-production timelines have compressed toward 2030 with strong Chinese policy backing.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Long-dated substitution risk to lithium-based chemistries.
insights.locator: Beyond LFP, alternative chemistries

insights.claim: Subsidy changes have stalled US EV momentum even as EV adoption accelerates across Europe and emerging markets.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Regional divergence in EV demand affects battery metal demand outlooks.
insights.locator: Battery technology and energy storage

insights.claim: Lithium carbonate prices rebounded about 130% from a multi-year low in mid-2025 to 2026, yet raw lithium carbonate is only 2% to 3% of total cost in a typical 100 MW, four-hour turnkey storage system.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Storage project economics are largely insensitive to lithium price swings.
insights.locator: Lithium carbonate prices fell to a multi-year low

insights.claim: An 83% lithium price rise in Q1 2026 translated into only a 9% increase in LFP cell prices and roughly 10% in turnkey system costs, with reference price lags of four to eight months adding insulation.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Lithium rallies have limited pass-through to storage buyers, capping demand destruction.
insights.locator: An 83% price rise in Q1 2026

insights.claim: Investors have put US$60 billion into the lithium supply chain over the past decade, producing a tenfold increase in refined chemical supply, and a further US$150 billion to US$250 billion is needed through the 2050s.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Large capital need underpins long-term lithium supply questions.
insights.locator: Investors have deployed US$60 billion

insights.claim: Chinese developers achieve significantly higher capital efficiency than Western counterparts, so Western markets need to broaden capital pools to build ex-China lithium supply chains and safeguard domestic automotive manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Ex-China lithium supply needs more capital per unit of capacity, which favours policy-backed financing.
insights.locator: Chinese developers achieve significantly higher capital efficiency

insights.claim: Across copper, aluminium, nickel and lithium, future supply depends on investment decisions made today, and security of supply, energy availability and geopolitics increasingly sit alongside cost competitiveness in shaping investment outcomes.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Strategic and political factors, not just cost, now drive where metals capital flows.
insights.quote: Across copper, aluminium, nickel and lithium, the common thread is that future supply depends on investment decisions being made today
insights.locator: Across copper, aluminium, nickel and lithium

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie says that without faster approvals and investment commitments the industry cannot deliver the mine supply needed to support future growth.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Permitting speed is a gating factor for the metals supply response.
insights.locator: High prices should trigger investment
